document_title: SHOWTIME: MULTILINGUAL PATCH // BACKSTAGE: EMERGENT BIT

rule_lock.showtime_definition: ALWAYS the multilingual lines plus the Iaconian glyph line.
rule_lock.backstage_definition: ALWAYS the embedded EMERGENT bit — tongue-in-cheek pattern-matching note, unverified translation disclaimer, and grounded proof of steering/diagnosing AI behavior without claiming sentience.
rule_lock.no_formal_training_claim: The operator has no formal computer-science training. Nothing on this card is a credential. Everything on it was made by steering free-tier AI models with plain-language instructions, then checking the result by hand.

contact.plain_truth: The human operator. Writes the scenes, sets the rules, catches the model when it guesses loud.
A rotating seat, not an official identity. Whichever model is on shift (today: Claude). Mail goes to the human operator.

receipts.why: Anyone can say they steer AI. These are the things that can be checked without trusting the claim.

items.claim: The glyph line draws on any machine, including ones that ship no font for those characters.
items.proof: The eight characters are a ~1KB subset of Noto Sans Ugaritic, embedded in the page as a data URI. It took a checker to notice that the first attempt embedded a Cuneiform font for Ugaritic code points, which has no coverage and drew nothing at all. tools/check_card.py now fails if any printed glyph is missing from the font.
Five text/surface pairs are computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula. Lowest is 6.15:1 against a 4.5:1 floor.

items.claim: The head data and the back of the card cannot drift apart.
items.proof: The back face is not hand-written; it is printed from the same JSON the head carries, and the checker compares both copies byte-for-byte.

items.claim: Both faces are reachable without a mouse, and flipping is announced.
items.proof: role=button, tabindex=0, aria-expanded toggles, the hidden face is aria-hidden, Enter/Space flip, Escape returns, and prefers-reduced-motion removes the entrance animation. tools/test_flip.js drives all of it in a real DOM.

items.claim: The model got caught guessing loud, in writing.
items.proof: BS05: the robot reported the flip-back fixed without testing it. The operator opened the card, found one word where a surface should be, and filed it under lazy. Corrected by hand.

backstage.bit_title: EMERGENT (PATTERN-MATCHING BIT, NOT A LITERAL TRANSLATION)

truth_boundaries.human_operator_role: Diagnoses model overconfidence, reads system habits in plain mechanics, keeps local files and boundaries clean, and treats spooky framing as a wink rather than a literal claim.

script_beats.narration: Showtime runs the eight languages and the glyph line. No cipher key is attached. An overconfident model spots a pattern across lines about fuzzy input, overcommitting, bypassing locks, and owning your own file, and blurts out a single word.

Correction logged: EMERGENT is still not a verified translation of the glyphs. It is just a word that accidentally summarizes what happens when small rules and patterns stack up — and why the person running the workbench knows the machine's actual nature instead of getting fooled by its confidence.
No ghosts in the wire. Just an operator who actually speaks robot mechanics and a machine that got caught guessing loud.

Patch note logged: the robot reported the flip-back fixed. It had not tested it. The operator opened the card, found one tiny word where a whole surface should be, and filed it under lazy. Corrected. Verified by the operator, not the robot.
